sections.h2: Where is West Des Moines and how big is it?
sections.html:
West Des Moines is a western suburb of Des Moines in central Iowa, and most of the city lies in Polk County. Parts extend into Dallas County, and small portions reach into Warren and Madison counties. The city sits in the Raccoon River valley.

The Census Bureau lists 47.22 square miles of land and 1,455.3 people per square mile for 2020. The 2020 census counted 68,723 residents, which made West Des Moines the sixth largest city in Iowa and the second largest in the Des Moines metro area. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 74,224.

sections.h2: Why was West Des Moines once called Valley Junction?
sections.html:
The town was incorporated as Valley Junction on October 9, 1893, and it kept that name until January 1, 1938. Voters approved the change to West Des Moines in a final election on December 7, 1937.

Settlement began on October 11, 1845, when James Cunningham Jordan fired a gunshot to declare the area open. His house is now a museum. The Rock Island railroad depot and shops shaped the early town, and a machinists' strike at those shops ran about 22 months in 1922 and 1923.

The city then grew by annexation: Clover Hills in 1950, Ashawa in 1957, Commerce in 1960 and land in Warren County in 2005. Because of that history, house age, lot size and street layout change a lot from one part of town to the next.

The old business district, Historic Valley Junction, was added to the National Register of Historic Places on October 11, 2017. The listing covers about 12 acres and 72 resources, of which 53 are contributing buildings, mostly one and two story brick.

sections.h2: What do Census Bureau figures say about West Des Moines housing?
sections.html:
For 2020 to 2024 the Census Bureau reports a median value of $309,000 for owner-occupied homes in West Des Moines and an owner-occupied rate of 57.4 percent. That leaves roughly 43 percent of households renting.

sections.h2: Who are the largest employers in West Des Moines?
sections.html:
Wells Fargo Home Mortgage and Credit Services is the largest employer, with about 9,000 workers listed in the city's 2023 annual financial report. Insurance and financial companies fill most of the rest of the list.

  • Athene USA Corporation: 1,665
  • Hy-Vee: 1,594
  • West Des Moines Community School District: 1,424
  • FBL Financial Group: 1,016
  • American Equity Investment Life: 889
  • Sammons Financial Group: 753
  • The Iowa Clinic: 669
  • Microsoft: 630

Hy-Vee, FBL Financial, GuideOne, American Equity, Sammons and ITA Group are all headquartered in the city. Microsoft runs several data centers here. Jordan Creek Town Center opened in 2004 and is described as the largest shopping mall in Iowa.

Owners who relocate for work, and heirs who live out of state, often prefer a quick closing to managing a house from a distance.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve West Des Moines homes?
sections.html:
Most of the city belongs to the West Des Moines Community School District. The part of the city in Dallas County belongs to the Waukee Community School District.

The West Des Moines district runs eight elementary schools, two junior highs, Valley High School, Valley Southwoods (a freshman high school) and the Walnut Creek Campus, an alternative high school. Dowling Catholic High School is among the private schools in the city.

Check the parcel record to see which district a house falls in, since the Dallas County edge of the city differs from the rest.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit work in West Des Moines?
sections.html:
Interstates 35, 80 and 235 all reach West Des Moines, and all three were built in the 1960s. Iowa Highway 28 forms much of the boundary with Des Moines.

Street numbers do not match Des Moines. Eighty-sixth Street in Clive becomes 22nd Street in West Des Moines. Des Moines Area Regional Transit provides bus service.

The Census Bureau puts the mean commute for West Des Moines workers at 18.3 minutes.

sections.h2: Does West Des Moines have flood risk?
sections.html:
Yes. The Raccoon River and Walnut Creek both have significant flood potential, and the city says so on its flood control page. After the Great Flood of 1993 a floodwall was built along Walnut Creek.

  • Clive, Des Moines and West Des Moines run the Des Moines Metro ALERT system, which uses rain and stream gauges to watch conditions and to operate the Raccoon River and Walnut Creek levee system.
  • A FEMA flood map is available for any address.
  • High groundwater often floods basements in spring, and owners are generally responsible for their sump pumps. The city says never to connect a sump pump to the sanitary sewer.
  • Sanitary sewer backups can be reported to Public Services at 515-222-3480.

Climate adds to the list. The January mean high is 26 degrees F, the July mean high is 86 degrees F, and annual precipitation is about 34.7 inches. A seller with a damp basement or an old sump setup should expect buyers to ask about it.

sections.h2: What city rules affect a West Des Moines house sale?
sections.html:
The rule most likely to affect a sale is rental licensing. West Des Moines requires rental properties to be licensed and inspected every two years by the Building Division, and any property not occupied by its owner counts as a rental, even when relatives who are not owners live there.

  • After an inspection, owners are told what repairs are required and generally have 30 days to finish them.
  • The Rental Housing Certificate is issued once fees are paid and repairs are done. It stays valid until the next inspection and can be transferred to a new owner.
  • It can be revoked if new violations appear between inspections and are not fixed.

Building permits are requested through the City Access Portal. The Development Services Department is at 4200 Mills Civic Parkway, and the Building Inspection office can be reached at 515-222-3630 or bi@wdm.iowa.gov. The pages we read do not describe a point-of-sale inspection, so ask the office before assuming either way.

sections.h2: Which county bills property tax on a West Des Moines house?
sections.html:
The county that bills a house is the county where its parcel sits, which is usually Polk and sometimes Dallas, Warren or Madison. Look up the parcel before you plan a closing.

Polk County mails statements once a year in late August. The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1, with late interest of 1.5 percent added on the first of each month after the grace date. Payments must carry a postmark by the due date. The Polk County Treasurer's phone is 515-286-3060.

Warren County, which holds a small part of the city, set its fiscal 2027 county levy at 5.64659 per $1,000 of taxable value for urban property, down from 5.84267 the year before. Taxes are normally prorated at closing, with the buyer credited for the seller's share, so check the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What does Iowa charge to record a West Des Moines deed?
sections.html:
Iowa charges a real estate transfer tax of 80 cents for each $500 of value above the first $500. The grantor, meaning the seller, is liable for it under Iowa Code 428A.3.

The county recorder collects the tax and will not record a taxable deed until it is paid. A declaration of value, signed by a buyer, seller or agent, goes in with the deed. Transfers with no consideration are exempt, including distributions to heirs, deeds given to a lender in lieu of foreclosure and transfers between spouses or between parent and child without actual consideration.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a West Des Moines house?
sections.html:
A West Des Moines owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or sell to a cash buyer, and each path trades time against effort.

  • List with an agent: the house is marketed and shown, but repairs, showings and buyer financing set the schedule.
  • Sell it yourself: you manage the listing, the paperwork and the price conversation.
  • Cash buyer: the house is bought as-is, and the closing date is set around your plans.

A cash sale can suit an inherited house, a rental with an expired certificate, or a property needing work. Tell us the address and the situation and we will respond with a written offer you are free to decline.

faqs.q: Is West Des Moines in Polk County or Dallas County?
faqs.a: Most of West Des Moines is in Polk County. Parts extend into Dallas County, and small portions are in Warren and Madison counties, so the parcel record decides which county bills a given house.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a West Des Moines house?
faqs.a: In Polk County the first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. Late interest of 1.5 percent is added on the first of each month after the grace date, and taxes are usually prorated between buyer and seller at closing.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a West Des Moines rental?
faqs.a: A rental needs a current license while it is rented. The city licenses and inspects rentals every two years, and the Rental Housing Certificate can be transferred to a new owner. Call 515-222-3630 to confirm where a certificate stands.

faqs.q: Who pays Iowa transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays. Iowa Code 428A.3 makes the person conveying the property liable, and the tax is 80 cents for each $500 above the first $500. Exempt transfers include distributions to heirs without consideration.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in West Des Moines that is in a flood area?
faqs.a: Yes. A FEMA flood map is available for any address, and buyers and lenders will look at it. Gather any past flood or sump pump information before you speak with buyers.
